PullRequest.Title: Add setting to open agent sessions in an editor
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.

Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/336136

Opening an agent session always shows it in the Chat view, replacing whatever the Chat view showed before. If you work with several sessions side by side, you then have to move each one into an editor by hand.

This adds an experimental setting, `chat.agentSessions.openInEditor` (off by default). When it is on, opening a session from the sessions list, a session picker, or an `agent-host-session:` link opens it in an editor, the same way opening a file does:

- A click opens the session in the active editor group; a modifier-click (Ctrl/Cmd) opens it in the side group.
- If an editor already shows the session, a click reveals that editor.
- If the session is currently shown in the Chat view, it moves into a new editor.

With the setting off, nothing changes.

## Implementation

- `openSessionDefault` in `agentSessionsOpener.ts` (sessions list and pickers) and the `agent-host-session:` link opener both target `ACTIVE_GROUP` when the setting is on, or `SIDE_GROUP` for a modifier-click. Without the setting, a modifier-click in the sessions list keeps opening an editor in the active group.
- `shouldRevealSessionEditor` decides whether an existing widget is revealed: only when it is an editor, not the Chat view.

## How to test

1. Set `"chat.agentSessions.openInEditor": true`.
2. Click a session in the Chat view's sessions list: it opens as an editor tab in the active editor group.
3. Click it again: the existing tab is revealed instead of opening a second one.
4. Ctrl/Cmd+click a session: it opens in the side group.
5. Open a session in the Chat view first, then click its link in a chat response: it moves into an editor.
6. Turn the setting off: sessions open in the Chat view as before.

## Validation

- `scripts\test.bat --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/agentSessions/agentSessionsOpener.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/agentSessions/agentHost/openSessionLinkOpener.contribution.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/attachments/chatReferenceAttachment.test.ts`: 32 passing. New tests cover the sessions list and session links with the setting on and off, modifier-clicks, and sessions already shown in the Chat view or in an editor.
- `npm run typecheck-client`: no errors in the changed files. The only error was in `terminalProcess.ts` and comes from a stale local `node-pty` install, unrelated to this change.
- Used daily in Code OSS for several days with sessions from local and remote agent hosts.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open an agent session from the sessions list or picker with the setting disabled or enabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The click marks the session read, waits for the session item provider activation and resolvability check, then opens either the existing Chat view path (setting disabled) or an editor in the active/side group (setting enabled). The destination UI must be ready before the open completes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Activate the extension-provided chat session item controller/content provider and resolve whether the session type is supported
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one item-provider activation and one resolvability check per open flow; already registered providers return without another extension activation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same activation and resolvability check ran before selecting ChatViewPaneTarget or ACTIVE_GROUP.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before the destination widget/editor opens.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open and initialize the Chat view or Chat editor, resolving the session model through its existing provider
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One destination host per selected session; existing matching editors are revealed rather than duplicated when revealIfOpened is true.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The default path initialized the Chat view; side-by-side and non-panel-resolvable sessions already used the same editor path. The opt-in setting intentionally chooses that existing editor path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: UI/model initialization is awaited before the open returns.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One selected session per user action. The added widget lookup is linear in currently instantiated chat widgets; editor reuse may scan open editor groups and tabs once. It does not scale with session-list size or message count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One awaited open flow per click. The diff adds no Promise fan-out, queue, subprocess burst, or parallel remote work; downstream provider activation retains existing service coordination.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm providers return from registered controller/content-provider state. Existing widgets and editor inputs are reused. On a cold provider, activation occurs exactly as before the diff; the configuration branch does not alter cache keys, negative caching, or coalescing.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that the changed branch adds only a configuration read and bounded in-memory widget lookup before the existing openSession path; repository tracing shows no new boundary or multiplicative work.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact number of open tabs/widgets and provider activation duration varies, but the added lookups are bounded by open UI surfaces and occur once per explicit open action.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. The editor behavior is opt-in, does not add boundary calls, and reuses/moves existing session state rather than constructing work per list item.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open an agent-host-session link, including a cold uncached authority and a warm known session
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The opener resolves the client session resource, strips a default-chat fragment if needed, activates the session item provider, then opens the Chat view or editor according to the setting/openToSide option.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: List sessions from the selected agent-host connection when the link cannot be resolved from registered identities
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One coalesced listSessions call per authority for concurrent cold misses; zero for known resources.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The identical resource resolution and listSessions operation occurred before the new configuration branch.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: A cold unresolved link waits for the list before opening; warm links avoid it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Activate the chat session item provider for the resolved resource type
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One activation request per link open, with registered providers returning from existing state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Activation was already awaited immediately before ChatViewPaneTarget/SIDE_GROUP selection.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One link per explicit open. A cold unresolved authority lists all sessions for that authority once; effective boundary cardinality remains one listSessions call regardless of returned session count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Concurrent cold resolutions for the same authority share _sessionListRefreshes. The diff does not change that coalescing or add concurrent editor opens.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: A known resource is resolved from IAgentHostConnectionsService without listing. Concurrent cold misses for one authority are coalesced; registered session identities make subsequent resolutions warm. The new setting is read only after resolution and provider activation, so it cannot defeat this cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the unchanged resolution/activation call path and the new branch occurring afterward.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Agent-host session counts and remote latency vary, but neither boundary's call count or placement changes in this PR.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. Cold remote work, warm caching, and same-authority coalescing are unchanged; destination selection adds only bounded in-memory lookup.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open a session already shown in the Chat view, in an editor, or in an inactive editor tab
Scenarios.CriticalPath: For an existing editor, the service reveals it. For a Chat-view session with editor targeting, it retains the model reference, clears/moves the source widget, and opens the editor. For an inactive tab without a widget, editor discovery reveals that input.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One selected resource. Widget discovery scans instantiated chat widgets once; editor discovery scans open groups/tabs at most once or along the existing reveal/move path. There is no history- or session-list-wide reconstruction.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Move and reveal operations are sequential and awaited. The model reference is retained until the destination acquires it, preventing duplicate asynchronous loads; no new burst is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing widgets/editor inputs are positive reuse states. Absence of a widget permits the editor service to find an inactive input. Session models are acquired from existing state during movement and released in finally; the diff introduces no persistent cache or retained key.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from shouldRevealSessionEditor and ChatWidgetService.openSession/prepareSessionForMove call tracing.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: A workspace can have many open tabs, but the scan is once per explicit open and is the existing editor-reuse mechanism; no evidence supports user-visible scaling regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. The changed logic avoids revealing the Chat view when the opt-in editor destination is requested and relies on existing model-transfer and editor-reuse lifecycle.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance review over all seven changed files and all diff pages. Traced list/picker opens, agent-host links, existing-editor reveal, Chat-view-to-editor moves, provider activation, remote session listing, cache/coalescing, and effective concurrency. No actionable performance issue was introduced, and the PR does not establish a concrete regression fix requiring blame attribution.
